report:
Reviewed the complete associated_identity claim, four ordinary implementation associations, and both ordinary tests. There are no TODO/N/A entries. Requirements are (1) distinct symbols for trait and impl functions, types, and constants, (2) association with their owner, (3) repeatable identity on requests, and (4) identity and owner preservation on sibling movement.

Implementation: associated.rs constructs a key from item kind, name, and occurrence within that kind/name. Both enumeration and semantic lowering call the same tracked local_trait_associated_item or local_impl_associated_item query keyed by owner plus this key. keyed_source_item searches kind/name occurrence rather than absolute sibling index. Thus inserting unrelated siblings or reordering differently named siblings does not change the minting query. lower_item builds each of the three concrete symbol variants with Some(owner); the associated fns.rs, type_aliases.rs, and consts.rs tracked structures store name, scope and owner as identity fields, with CST and span tracked separately. Their distinct variants and per-owner minting query preserve item identity, while placement updates alter only span/CST fields. Same-kind/name duplicate declarations are disambiguated by occurrence; the claim does not assign persistent identity to otherwise indistinguishable duplicate declarations under an exchange of duplicates.

Tests: trait_items_have_stable_symbols_and_owner_identity obtains methods, an associated function, a type and constant from a trait; explicitly asserts the function/type/constant owner and compares all semantic symbols with a second independent membership enumeration. This checks repeated retrieval through both access paths produces the same symbols. Its extra signature and binder assertions concern other anchors and do not substitute for identity evidence. moving_associated_items_preserves_symbol_query_keys exercises all six owner-kind combinations, first inserting a preceding sibling, then separately reordering siblings, and reversing each edit. Its nested helper explicitly asserts each selected local symbol's owner and invokes a tracked identity observer for the target. Each forward and reverse revision asserts that observer does not execute again. Captured ObservedSymbol interning keys on the symbol itself and the observer has no detail dependencies; captured database logging records WillExecute and clears between observations. A reminted target would create a new observer input and execute, failing these assertions. Captured fixture helpers establish one persistent database/source and recreate the root through a tracked setup query. The tests therefore cover the ownership and stability claim with visible assertions, not merely annotation names.

Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness associated_items_preserves_symbol_query_keys -- --nocapture: the one selected movement test passed. Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness trait_items_have_stable_symbols_and_owner_identity -- --nocapture successfully, and confirmed with the exact lib test invocation: one owner-identity test passed. Existing compiler warnings were unrelated. Additional source dependencies were captured with review read (fixture setup, identity observer, database creation/query logging and review policy). No production or test changes were required.
